chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Ubayd ibn Zurara who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about what a man may own from among his relatives. He said: He cannot own his father, nor his mother, nor his sister, nor a daughter of his brother, nor a daughter of his sister, nor his paternal aunt, nor his maternal aunt; and he may own what is besides that from among the men from his relatives, and he cannot own his mother through the nursing (relationship).

key_terms.الرَّضَاعَةِ: Nursing/breastfeeding relationship; creates legal kinship comparable to blood relations in Islamic law
key_terms.ذَوِي قَرَابَتِهِ: His relatives/kinship group; those connected through blood ties
key_terms.يَمْلِكُ: To own/possess as property; in classical fiqh, refers to acquiring a person as a slave

ai.seo_question: Which relatives is a man forbidden from owning as slaves according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the categories of relatives whom a man is prohibited from holding in slavery. The ruling enumerates specific female relatives (mother, sister, niece through brother, niece through sister, paternal aunt, maternal aunt) as permanently exempt from ownership, along with the milk-mother. While male relatives in general may be owned as slaves under classical Islamic law, the Imam clarifies that female kin within specified degrees of kinship cannot be acquired in this manner, protecting them from exploitation within the family structure.
